source.title: PODCAST MREŽNICA: Andrijanić: Berlin želi kontrolu Poljske, Tusk ima zadaću.Ovo je pouka i Hrvatskoj

summary.title_hr: PODCAST MREŽNICA: Andrijanić: Berlin želi kontrolu Poljske, Tusk ima zadaću. Ovo je pouka i Hrvatskoj
summary.abstract_hr: U podcastu Mrežnica voditeljica razgovara s hrvatsko-poljskim novinarom Goranom Andrijanićem, koji se javlja iz Varšave, o političkoj krizi u Poljskoj nakon slanja policije u Ustavni sud. Andrijanić opisuje dugogodišnji sukob konzervativnog tabora okupljenog oko Prava i pravde i predsjednika Karola Nawrockog s vladom premijera Donalda Tuska. Taj sukob tumači kao borbu suverenista i globalista u kojoj, prema njegovu mišljenju, Tusk provodi njemačke interese. Razgovor obuhvaća spor oko Ustavnog suda, gospodarske prilike, poljske zlatne rezerve, pobačaj, izostanak lustracije te odnos prema Rusiji i Njemačkoj. Na kraju gost kritizira šutnju hrvatskih konzervativnih stranaka i ističe pouke za Hrvatsku: čuvanje srednjoeuropskog identiteta, naoružavanje i Inicijativu triju mora.
key_points: Andrijanić slanje policije u Ustavni sud smatra oblikom državnog udara. Ističe da je spor oko suda trajao oko petnaest godina, ali je dosad ostajao unutar demokratskih okvira, dok za ovaj potez prema njegovim riječima ne postoji nikakva zakonska osnova.

Gost tvrdi da je Nawrocki pri odbijanju prisege ustavnih sudaca djelovao unutar zakonskog okvira, iako možda nategnutog. Tuskov tabor je, s druge strane, organizirao polaganje prisege bez predsjednika, a sutkinja koja još nije prisegnula suspendirala je predsjednika i potpredsjednika suda.

Prema Andrijaniću, akcija je namjerno tempirana za blagdan Svih svetih, dok je predsjednik letio prema Senegalu. Nawrocki je nad Gibraltarom okrenuo zrakoplov i osobno se probio do Ustavnog suda. Glasine o sudjelovanju njemačke policije gost je opovrgnuo.

Gost sukob opisuje kao borbu suverenističkog i globalističkog koncepta. Tusk je prema njemu politički štićenik Angele Merkel koji slijedi njemačke interese, zbog čega su usporeni gospodarski rast i veliki projekti poput središnjeg prometnog čvora između Łódźa i Varšave.

Andrijanić navodi da je Poljska u gospodarskoj krizi s velikim deficitom, rastućom nezaposlenošću i zdravstvenim sustavom u raspadu. Upozorava i na pokušaje da se guverner središnje banke Adam Głapiński izvede pred Državni sud te na Tuskov interes za poljske zlatne rezerve i uvođenje eura.

Gost ističe da Poljska nije provela lustraciju, uz napomenu da je dokazano kako je Lech Wałęsa početkom sedamdesetih surađivao s komunističkim službama. Rusiju smatra najvećom sigurnosnom prijetnjom Poljskoj i Europi, ali poljsko-ruski sukob kratkoročno ne vidi kao realan.

Andrijanić kritizira šutnju hrvatskih konzervativnih i suverenističkih stranaka o događajima u Poljskoj, za razliku od Janeza Janše. Kao pouke za Hrvatsku navodi čuvanje srednjoeuropskog identiteta, vlastito naoružavanje i oslonac na Inicijativu triju mora.

key_points_en: Andrijanić considers sending police into the Constitutional Tribunal to be a form of coup d'état. He points out that the dispute over the court lasted about fifteen years, but until now remained within democratic frameworks, whereas for this move, according to his words, no legal basis exists whatsoever.

The guest claims that Nawrocki acted within the legal framework, although perhaps stretched, when refusing the oath of constitutional judges. Tusk's camp, on the other hand, organized the taking of the oath without the president, and a judge who had not yet taken the oath suspended the president and vice president of the court.

According to Andrijanić, the action was deliberately timed for the feast of All Saints, while the president was flying toward Senegal. Nawrocki turned the aircraft around over Gibraltar and personally made his way to the Constitutional Tribunal. Rumors about the participation of German police were denied by the guest.

The guest describes the conflict as a struggle between the sovereignist and globalist concepts. According to him, Tusk is a political protégé of Angela Merkel who pursues German interests, which is why economic growth and large projects such as the central transport hub between Łódź and Warsaw have slowed down.

Andrijanić states that Poland is in an economic crisis with a large deficit, rising unemployment, and a healthcare system in collapse. He also warns of attempts to bring central bank governor Adam Głapiński before the State Tribunal, as well as Tusk's interest in Polish gold reserves and the introduction of the euro.

The guest points out that Poland did not carry out lustration, noting that it has been proven that Lech Wałęsa collaborated with communist services in the early seventies. He considers Russia the greatest security threat to Poland and Europe, but does not see a Polish-Russian conflict as realistic in the short term.

Andrijanić criticizes the silence of Croatian conservative and sovereignist parties regarding the events in Poland, unlike Janez Janša. As lessons for Croatia, he cites preserving Central European identity, own armament, and reliance on the Three Seas Initiative.

summary.title_en: PODCAST MREŽNICA: Andrijanić: Berlin wants control of Poland, Tusk has an assignment. This is a lesson for Croatia as well
summary.abstract_en: In the Mrežnica podcast, the host talks with Croatian-Polish journalist Goran Andrijanić, reporting from Warsaw, about the political crisis in Poland after police were sent into the Constitutional Tribunal. Andrijanić describes the years-long conflict between the conservative camp gathered around Law and Justice and President Karol Nawrocki and the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. He interprets this conflict as a struggle between sovereignists and globalists in which, in his view, Tusk is carrying out German interests. The conversation covers the dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal, economic conditions, Polish gold reserves, abortion, the lack of lustration, and the relationship toward Russia and Germany. In the end, the guest criticizes the silence of Croatian conservative parties and highlights lessons for Croatia: preserving Central European identity, armament, and the Three Seas Initiative.
